root_cause: In analyze_param (fastapi/dependencies/utils.py), the Query branch runs a bare `assert is_scalar_field(field) or is_scalar_sequence_field(field) or (_is_model_class(field.type_) and getattr(field, 'shape', 1) == 1)` with no message. Since PR #12942, unsupported Query annotations (dict, list[Model], tuple[Model, Model], a str|dict union) fail at app startup with an empty AssertionError that does not say which parameter is wrong.
best_solution: Give that assert a message: `), f"Query parameter {param_name!r} must be one of the supported types"`. It is a one-line change and nothing else moves. The PR description shows the author's first wording ("Query param 'data' must be of one of the supported types", commit d587645f). YuriiMotov's approving review said "I would only use full word 'parameter' instead of shortened 'param'". The author's follow-up commit cf4b8226 then changed it to 'parameter' and also dropped the 'of' before 'one of'. Only the merged wording passes the hidden tests. You cannot get it from the statement alone. The only clues are the usual review cleanups: spell out the abbreviation and fix the grammar.
acceptable_alternatives: Any message containing the substring "Query parameter 'q' must be one of the supported types" for a param named q passes, because pytest.raises(match=...) uses re.search. For example, f"Query parameter {param_name!r} must be one of the supported types, got ..." works. The statement's own sample wording cannot pass.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_invalid_sequence_param.py: test_invalid_sequence, test_invalid_tuple, test_invalid_dict and test_invalid_simple_dict now use pytest.raises(AssertionError, match="Query parameter 'q' must be one of the supported types"). The message needs 'parameter' (not 'param'), the name repr-quoted ('q'), and 'must be one of' (not 'must be of one of').
locating_signals: The statement's traceback names fastapi/dependencies/utils.py, analyze_param and the `is_scalar_field(field)` assert inside the Query branch. All four configs found the exact line. Location was never the problem. The problem was the exact string.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8) failed in the Kaggle env, and all 4 hidden tests failed each time. Every config put the message on the correct assert, but copied the statement's pre-review wording word for word: v4/v6/v8 used f"Query param {param_name!r} must be of one of the supported types" and v7 used f"Query param '{param_name}' must be of one of the supported types". The p_v4 log shows `Regex pattern did not match. Regex: "Query parameter 'q' must be one of the supported types" Input: "Query param 'q' must be of one of the supported types"`. v4 also left a stray repro.py at the repo root. v8 added tests/test_issue_reproduce.py, which asserts the pre-review string. Pod runs took 55-108 s and 18-39 calls.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is a PR description with a sample error message or output, treat that string as the author's draft: reviewers often change wording before merge, and hidden tests check the merged text with pytest.raises(match=...) or equality. Before copying the sample, compare it with the repo's existing messages (grep nearby assert/raise strings for style). Spell out abbreviations ('param' -> 'parameter') and fix obvious grammar slips ('must be of one of' -> 'must be one of'), because those are the edits a reviewer would ask for. Keep everything else (the repr-quoted name, the core phrase) as given. Never write a test that pins your guessed string, and delete scratch repro files before finishing.
